name: Korg KRONOS EXi Program
description: Korg KRONOS, KRONOS 2 and KRONOS 3: a program of an EXi bank (AL-1, CX-3, STR-1, MS-20EX, PolysixEX, MOD-7, SGX-2, EP-1 in either slot) by SysEx parameter change, its common settings read back from the current program.

authoringNotes: Generated by tools/profiles/korg/make-profiles.mjs; edit the layout in tools/profiles/korg/synths/, not this file.

Every row of Prog_EXi_Common.txt with a parameter id is a parameter, named by its group and its name as printed, and sent by Parameter Change (function 43): F0 42 3g 68 43 TYP SOC SUB PID IDX and the value as 21 bits, two's complement, high byte first (*4). Nothing here has been sent to a real instrument yet.

The rows of KARMA… go by KARMA Parameter Change (function 6D), the same message as Parameter Change under another code. The table prints no message per row. Per group, the rows whose ids Parameter Change also takes for another row, and so cannot go by it: KARMA Common, 25 of 527 (0 0 0 3 0 is KARMA Common Latch Switch and Common Legato); KARMA Module, 13 of 219 (1 0 0 0 0 is KARMA Module GE Number and Common LFO Waveform). A group with such rows cannot go by Parameter Change; one with none goes by 6D on the message's name alone. A reading, not tried on an instrument.

The rows of Drum Track… go by Drum Track Parameter Change (function 6E), the same message as Parameter Change under another code. The table prints no message per row. Per group, the rows whose ids Parameter Change also takes for another row, and so cannot go by it: Drum Track Common, 9 of 11 (0 0 0 1 0 is Drum Track Common Pattern Number and Common Assign Mode); Drum Track, 0 of 22. A group with such rows cannot go by Parameter Change; one with none goes by 6E on the message's name alone. A reading, not tried on an instrument.

A program of an EXi bank: its two EXi slots, each with the settings of every engine it can hold, and its effects, KARMA and controllers. An HD-1 program is korg-kronos. The KRONOS takes program parameters in Program mode ("Which parameters are currently available for editing depends on the instrument's mode").

The effects' own parameters: 1072 for the 16 effect slots, a parameter per pid of Effect.txt (`Insert Effect1 Parameter 5`), sent by Parameter Change as TYP 6 with the slot in SOC and the pid in PID. The table's effect switch goes out as that address with pid 0 (`6 0 0 0 0`, `* -> bypass`), and pid 0 is Bypass in every type, which the builder checks: TYP 6 is read as the effects' own parameters, a reading, not tried on an instrument. A pid means what the slot's effect type makes it (its description gives some), so its range is the widest any type gives it, and it is not read back: each type lays the slot's bytes out its own way. Effect Type is a choice of the 186 types its range 0~185 reaches; Effect.txt also lists 12 beyond it (186 Small Phase, 187 Orange Phase, …), outside the range the table prints, and not offered.

A range whose first value is the larger (9D~63) is two's complement over its bytes, -99~+99. A choice is a row naming both of two values. The value column is 19 characters wide; a name it cuts short keeps its cut, with an ellipsis. Other value names are in each parameter's description.
A parameter id above 126 takes the message's second form, 7F PIDH PIDL, which the archive calls deprecated and says the instrument still receives.

The EXi engines' own settings come from Prog_EXi.txt (each engine's rows as many as its heading prints: AL-1 609, CX-3 151, STR-1 707, MS-20EX 512, PolysixEX 322, MOD-7 1108, SGX-2 23, EP-1 183), once for each slot: EXi1 by TYP 11, EXi2 by TYP 12, as the program table's own rows for each slot take them (EXi1 Mod.Mixer1 Type, TYP 11, EXi2 Mod.Mixer1 Type, TYP 12) and the voice model files say ("<type> 0B: EXi patch 1, 0C: EXi patch 2"). A slot takes the settings of the engine in it: another engine's are refused or mean something else, and engines share ids, so a message from the instrument that more than one engine's setting sends is not attributed to any.
Read and not sent: EXi1 Common Algorithm Type, EXi2 Common Algorithm Type; the table prints no parameter id for them.
792 rows with an id print a fixed value (`10(fixed)`, `00(fixed)`: Insert Effect1 Channel; Insert Effect2 Channel; Insert Effect3 Channel; …) and are not settings.

Left out: 21 settings (Insert Effect1 Chain Switch; Insert Effect1 Chain To; Insert Effect2 Chain Switch; Insert Effect2 Chain To; Insert Effect3 Chain Switch; Insert Effect3 Chain To; …): shares its parameter id with Chain To (`* Chain To`), and the archive does not say which value of it turns the chain off.

Left out: 2 settings (Master Effect Chain Switch; Master Effect Chain Level): the table prints one id for Master Effect Chain Switch and Master Effect Chain Level, unmarked, and does not say which value means which.

Left out: 8 settings (KARMA Common (RT Param.1) Param.Assign; KARMA Common (RT Param.2) Param.Assign; KARMA Common (RT Param.3) Param.Assign; KARMA Common (RT Param.4) Param.Assign; KARMA Common (RT Param.5) Param.Assign; KARMA Common (RT Param.6) Param.Assign; …): no range printed (data(hex) is blank).
Left out: 1 setting (KARMA Module Start Seed): a 32-bit value in four bytes with an id each (`* Big Endian`), wider than a 21-bit parameter change.

Left out: 33 settings (Tone Adjust Knob1 Assign; Tone Adjust Knob2 Assign; Tone Adjust Knob3 Assign; Tone Adjust Knob4 Assign; Tone Adjust Knob5 Assign; Tone Adjust Knob6 Assign; …): its parameter change takes SUB from the value (`SUB = (Assign >> 7) & 0x01, Value = Assign & 0x7f`), which one message template cannot.

Left out: 16 settings (EXi1 STR-1 [PCM] High MS Bank UUID; EXi1 STR-1 [PCM] Mid High MS Bank UUID; EXi1 STR-1 [PCM] Mid Low MS Bank UUID; EXi1 STR-1 [PCM] Low MS Bank UUID; EXi2 STR-1 [PCM] High MS Bank UUID; EXi2 STR-1 [PCM] Mid High MS Bank UUID; …): a 16-byte UUID, sent by Parameter Change (binary), function 44.

Left out: 200 settings (EXi1 EP-1 [IFX Small Phaser] Bypass; EXi1 EP-1 [IFX Small Phaser] WetDry; EXi1 EP-1 [IFX Small Phaser] WetDry D.Mod Source; EXi1 EP-1 [IFX Small Phaser] WetDry D.Mod Intensity; EXi1 EP-1 [IFX Small Phaser] Input Trim; EXi1 EP-1 [IFX Small Phaser] Speed; …): EP-1 prints the same ids for the settings of 8 blocks ([IFX Small Phaser], [IFX Orange Black Phaser], [IFX Vintage Chorus], [IFX Black Chorus], [IFX EP Chorus], [IFX Vintage Flanger], [IFX Red Comp], [IFX Vox Wah]), one meaning per block chosen.

Pull: Current Object Dump Request (function 74) for object 00, the program, answered by a Current Object Dump (function 75) carrying object version 5 and 4960 bytes in Korg's 8-in-7 packing (*3: 5669 bytes). 8005 parameters are read back at their rows' offsets and bits. A dump of any other length does not match: an HD-1 program, laid out otherwise, comes back under the same header.

Byte order: a value over whole bytes is read low byte first, and a field that runs on into the next byte has its low bits in the earlier one. The tables fill each byte from bit 0 upward (every effect's Bypass is bit 0 of its first byte, Wet/Dry bits 7~1 beside it), and a field crossing a byte continues upward in the next (an EXi engine's [LFO1] Start Phase at bits 7~5, then 3~0): the layout of a little-endian structure. The one exception the archive marks, the KARMA Start Seed (`* Big Endian`), is left out. A reading, not tried on an instrument.

The EXi engines' settings are read back from each slot's engine block, at their Prog_EXi.txt offset from its start: EXi1 bytes 2908~3908, starting 51 bytes after its Algorithm Type; EXi2 bytes 3960~4959, starting 51 bytes after its Algorithm Type. The program table prints the blocks as reserved bytes, and does not say where an engine's table starts in its slot's; read here as at the run's start, the same distance from the Algorithm Type in both slots, every engine's table fitting (the longest reaches byte 998 of it). A reading, not tried on an instrument. A setting is read only when its slot's Algorithm Type holds its engine (the mapping's `when`).

Sent and not read back: 128 settings (KARMA Common (Note Map) C-1; KARMA Common (Note Map) C#-1; KARMA Common (Note Map) D-1; KARMA Common (Note Map) D#-1; KARMA Common (Note Map) E-1; KARMA Common (Note Map) F-1; …): a value the dump may hold as FF, which the parameter does not offer.
The exclusive header carries the global MIDI channel as 3g; the profile's deviceId variable is that byte, 30H for channel 1.

Identity: the Device Inquiry reply (KRONOS_MIDI_Implementation.pdf) is printed F0 7E 0g 06 02 42 68 00 mm 00 vv ww xx 00 F7. Its 7th to 8th bytes, 68 00, are checked as printed, where the universal reply puts the family code; its 9th byte, mm, is one per model and is not checked: KRONOS/KRONOS2 61Keys 05H, KRONOS/KRONOS2 73Keys 0EH, KRONOS/KRONOS2 88Keys 17H, KRONOS3 61Keys 1DH, KRONOS3 73Keys 26H, KRONOS3 88Keys 2FH.

Preset recall: Bank Select MSB and LSB, then Program Change, for the 31 banks the implementation's receive table gives in Program mode when Global's Bank Map is KORG (INT-A, INT-B, INT-C, INT-D, INT-E, INT-F, USER-A, USER-B, USER-C, USER-D, USER-E, USER-F, USER-G, USER-AA, USER-BB, USER-CC, USER-DD, USER-EE, USER-FF, USER-GG, G (001-128), g(1) (001-128), g(2) (001-128), g(3) (001-128), g(4) (001-128), g(5) (001-128), g(6) (001-128), g(7) (001-128), g(8) (001-128), g(9) (001-128), g(d) (001-128)). The banks numbered 001-128 are the GM ones, read-only (KRONOS_MIDI_SysEx.txt *2: "GM, g(1)-g(9), g(d) (read-only)"). The table also reaches some of them by a second select (38,00 (G), 3E,00 (g(d))), not offered. With Bank Map GM(2) the MSBs differ, and this recall does not apply.
